items.title: CrossContextsSettings
items.text: This MODX Extra adds a custom manager page where you can edit the settings of different contexts in one place. With this extra it is possible to compare the settings of the contexts in a single view.

items.title: Requirements
items.text:
• MODX Revolution 2.7+
  • PHP 7.2+

items.title: Features
items.text:
• Tabular view of all settings in all contexts
  • The displayed contexts can be restricted with a system settings
  • Create one setting in different contexts in one step

items.title: License

items.title: Translations
items.text: Translations of the package can be made for the Default Lexicon and the System Setting Lexicon

items.title: Install from MODX Extras
items.text: Search for CrossContextsSettings in the Package Manager of your MODX installation and install it in there.

items.title: Manual installation
items.text:
If you can't access the MODX Extras Repository in your MODX installation, you can manually install CrossContextsSettings.

  • Download the transport package from MODX Extras (or one of the pre built transport packages in _packages)
  • Upload the zip file to your MODX installation's core/packages folder or upload it manually in the MODX Package Manager.
  • In the MODX Manager, navigate to the Package Manager page, and select 'Search locally for packages' from the dropdown button.
  • CrossContextsSettings should now show up in the list of available packages. Click the corresponding 'Install' button and follow the instructions to complete the installation.

items.title: Build it from source
items.text: To build and install the package from source you could use Git Package Management. The GitHub repository of CrossContextsSettings contains a config.json to build that package locally. Use this option, if you want to debug CrossContextsSettings and/or contribute bugfixes and enhancements.

items.title: Custom Manager Page
items.text:
To use the component, navigate to your manager and click on "Extras > CrossContextsSettings".

You could create a new context setting in several contexts with a click on the Create New Setting button on the top left above the contexts settings grid.

The grid could be filtered by the namespace, the area and with a search input on the top right above the cronjob grid.

Each context setting can be edited inline with a double click on the text of the setting.

items.title: Create
items.text:
The context setting create window has a variety of options that can be set.

You could set the setting key, the setting name, the setting description, the setting field type, the setting namespace and the setting area. The fields in that window are the same as in the default context setting create/edit window.

The values of each context setting can be filled below those fields in a (sometimes scrollable) section. Each possible context setting is listed there with Value (context name):

items.title: Clear Cache
items.text: The clear cache tab allows you to clear any context cache manually.

items.title: Settings
items.text:
The settings tab allows you to edit the system settings of CrossContextsSettings.

CrossContextsSettings uses the following system settings in the namespace crosscontextssettings:

Key Name Description Default crosscontextssettings.clear_cache Clear Context Cache Clear the context cache after modifying an entry. No crosscontextssettings.contexts Contexts Comma-separated list of contexts displayed in the custom manager page. No value means that all contexts are displayed. - crosscontextssettings.debug Debug Log debug information in the MODX error log. No
